renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: He is not nine selves. Not a pile of words. Not a god with three heads. Not sounds, not moon-pieces, not wheels. Cross every one of those out.
The scary stuff is only scary for sleepy minds — like a mother making faces to keep a small child walking. He has no direction, no time, no number. You can't point at him, and you can't tell him.
His joy is the taste of your own self, full-formed in the goddess. His body fills the world and stays clean. So who does the worshipping here, and who gets pleased?
Sing her as she is: the highest goddess in highest form. Power and the powerful are not two things — the highest power of the highest self.
Fire burns and is never separate from its burning — stepping in is what starts it, in knowing, in being. Stepped into power, undivided, one-track mind: formed as Śiva, named as his goddess.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: Not nine. Not a word-pile. Not a three-headed statue. Not hums, not moon-chunks, not wheels. Delete all of it.
The horror stuff is for minds that haven't woken up — mom making monster faces so you keep walking. No location, no clock, no count. Unpointable. Untellable.
The joy is an inside taste — your own self, full cup, goddess pour. Body so clean it fills the world. Which begs it: who is worshipping and who is getting worshipped.
Sing it straight: highest goddess, highest form. Power and powerful, zero gap — top power of the top self.
Fire and burning were never two things. Entry is what starts it — in knowing, in being. Locked in, undivided, one-track mind: Śiva-formed, goddess-named.
